messages:
ada (design): quick design check from yesterday's review: users get tripped up by two things — the inline validation on rule conditions (it shows a red dot but no helpful text) and the preview button that sometimes stays disabled with no explanation. thoughts?
tom (pm): agree. we need clearer validation messages and disabled-state affordances. propose: show inline message under the condition field: 'Invalid expression: missing matcher' and show tooltip on the red dot explaining the error. For preview disabled, surface a reason: 'Preview unavailable: no snapshot selected' or 'Preview paused: simulation budget exceeded'.
noah (frontend): implementation notes: the condition editor is a thin code-like input. adding inline text is fine but watch vertical rhythm. we can collapse the helper text when the field is empty to avoid noise. for the red dot tooltip, we'll use aria-describedby to link the dot to the error text.
sara (a11y): accessibility points:
  - error messages must be programmatically associated with fields (aria-describedby) and announced on blur/change when the error appears.
  - disabled preview button should include aria-disabled="true" and a visible explanation (sr-only) like 'Preview disabled because no snapshot is selected'.
  - avoid only color indicators for validation; the red dot must have text equivalent.
ada (design): small copy suggestion: instead of 'Invalid expression' try 'Incomplete rule condition' — it's less technical for product managers reviewing policies. then sub-copy: 'Add a matcher (equals, contains) and a value.'
tom (pm): good tone. also we had a usability test where users couldn't find the reorder affordance for priorities. current icon is small and only visible on hover. propose we show a slightly larger handle and add a short affordance text 'Drag to reorder' visible on hover and sr-only always.
noah (frontend): note: showing the handle always increases visual clutter. compromise: make it 24px, low-contrast when idle, full contrast on hover/focus. add sr-only instructions point for keyboard move: 'press space to pick up, use arrow keys to move, press space to drop'. i'll implement keyboard reordering using roving tabindex and live updates to aria-live polite announcing new position.
sara (a11y): nit: when announcing position, avoid announcing raw index only. say 'Rule "Block suspicious IPs" moved to position 2 of 5'. include rule name for clarity. also ensure the live region updates are debounced to avoid too frequent announcements during rapid moves.
tom (pm): validation UX: we should surface a summary at top of rules list if any rule has a blocking validation error: a small banner '1 rule has errors: fix to enable simulation' with a 'Show errors' link that expands a panel listing issues. owner: ada for copy + design.
oah (frontend): plan: add top banner when validations exist, anchor links to jump to field, and include a small inline chevron to expand the details. will add tests in storybook for the banner + expanded list. ETA next week.
ci-bot: pipeline queued for branch feature/routing-validation-hints  status: pending.
ada (design): one more tiny thing: localization. our error copy will need to be short and pattern-based so translators can reuse tokens. i'll draft parenthetical tokens: e.g., '{field} is required' -> 'Condition field is required'.
sara (a11y): final checklist for PR: aria-describedby for errors, role=status polite live region for non-critical updates (counts, positions), role=alert for critical blockers, keyboard focus order for expanded errors panel, ensure error banner receives focus when inserted.
tom (pm): summary action items:
  - ada: finalize copy + error banner mockups
  - noah: implement inline messages, tooltip for dot, disabled preview explanations, larger drag handle + keyboard reordering announcements
  - sara: review a11y PR + checklist
  - i'll add these to the sprint ticket and schedule a quick recon after the PR lands
noah (frontend): starting work today. will push a small storybook PR first for review.
ada (design): thanks, will attach mocks to the ticket.
